Fix CSS build in deployment by using correct Tailwind v4 CLI

The project uses Tailwind CSS v4 syntax (@import, @source, @plugin
directives) but the build commands were using the old v3 CLI which
doesn't process v4 syntax correctly, causing CSS changes to not appear
in deployed builds.

Updated Dockerfile and CI workflows to use @tailwindcss/cli instead of
the legacy tailwindcss command, and removed the obsolete -c config flag
since v4 uses @config directive in the CSS file.

Use npx tailwindcss instead of @tailwindcss/cli for v4 compatibility

The tailwindcss package (v4.1.13) in devDependencies is the correct CLI
for Tailwind v4. Using @tailwindcss/cli was unnecessarily specific and
may have caused issues in the Docker build environment.

This ensures the CSS with all custom utilities (surface-raised, etc.)
builds correctly in production.

Fix onboarding projects redirecting to missing project permission (#257)

The sessionAndProject function had a bug where ONBOARDING projects
were incorrectly redirected to /?missingProjectPermission even when
the user had valid access.

The issue was in the pattern matching logic:
1. Pattern `Just p | p.paymentPlan /= "ONBOARDING"` correctly skipped
   ONBOARDING projects
2. But the fallthrough `_ | pid == nil || isSudo` only allowed nil
   UUIDs or sudo users to fetch from DB
3. Regular users with ONBOARDING projects fell through to the redirect

This fix adds an explicit pattern for ONBOARDING projects (Just _)
that fetches fresh data from the database, matching the original
intent described in the comments.

Support more KQL operators and functions (#259)

* Add KQL functions for _overview.yaml SQL migration

Implement P0 and P1 KQL features needed to migrate _overview.yaml dashboard
queries from SQL to KQL:

P0 Features:
- countif(condition): COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE condition) for error rate calculations
- dcount(field): COUNT(DISTINCT field) for service/resource counts

P1 Features:
- coalesce(field, default): COALESCE for null handling
- strcat(field1, separator, field2): CONCAT for string concatenation
- iff(condition, then, else): CASE WHEN for simple conditionals
- case(cond1, val1, ..., default): Multi-branch CASE for categorization

SQL generation for each function:
- countif(status == "ERROR") → COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'ERROR')
- dcount(service_name) → COUNT(DISTINCT service_name)
- coalesce(method, "unknown") → COALESCE(method, 'unknown')
- strcat(method, " ", path) → CONCAT(method, ' ', path)
- iff(x > 0, a, b) → CASE WHEN x > 0 THEN a ELSE b END
- case(x >= 500, e, x >= 400, w, s) → CASE WHEN x >= 500 THEN e WHEN x >= 400 THEN w ELSE s END

Example target KQL for _overview.yaml:
  kind == "server" AND duration != null
  | summarize
      error_rate = countif(status_code == "ERROR") * 100.0 / count(),
      p95_latency = percentile(duration / 1e6, 95)
    by resource.service.name

Move trace tree building from client to server (#317)

* Move trace tree building from client to server

Build trace adjacency maps (TraceTreeEntry) server-side in Haskell and
send them as part of the JSON response, replacing the client-side
grouping/orphan/virtual-parent logic in JS. This simplifies the frontend
considerably and makes trace structure deterministic.

* Auto-format code with fourmolu

* Fix hlint warnings across codebase

* Auto-format code with fourmolu

* Fix trace tree dropping nested spans by using parent-child relationships

buildTraceTree was using positional queryResultCount to determine roots,
which excluded query result rows from parent-child linking. Now a span is
a root only when its parent is absent from the data, and all spans with
in-data parents are properly linked as children.

* Fix non-query-result spans appearing as roots in trace tree

Use query-result-aware root selection: only QR spans whose parent is
not also a QR span become roots. This prevents non-matching ancestor
spans (e.g. user_add_to_cart when querying method=="GET") from
appearing at root level, while preserving full tree nesting when all
spans in a trace are query results.

* add kind to queries

* Restore parent_id IS NOT NULL filter in child spans query

With QR-based root selection, root spans (parent_id=NULL) from
selectChildSpansAndLogs are never tree roots and never reachable
from QR subtrees. Restoring the filter reduces the result set size.

fix(notify): atomically claim error re-notifications to prevent dupes

When traffic spiked and multiple ProcessProjectErrorsJob rows landed within
seconds, all concurrent workers ran queryDueErrorNotifications, saw the same
"due" rows (last_notified_at wasn't updated until after the send), and all
fired. Slack received 10 identical "Still firing" messages in 5.7s for the
same issue.

Replace the read-then-write flow with a CTE+UPDATE compare-and-swap:

  WITH candidates AS (SELECT ... cadence predicates ...)
  UPDATE error_patterns SET last_notified_at = now()
  FROM candidates c
  WHERE e.id = c.id
    AND e.last_notified_at IS NOT DISTINCT FROM c.last_notified_at
  RETURNING ...;

Under read-committed, only the first worker's CAS succeeds; losers get zero
rows back and skip dispatch entirely. No locks, no schema change.

Preserves the rate-limit retry semantic: on consumeNotificationToken denial,
revertLastNotifiedAt restores the pre-claim value so the next tick is eligible.
Post-send only persists slack/discord thread IDs now — last_notified_at is
already stamped by the claim.

fix(billing): split usage report into chunks and decouple bookkeeping from provider submission

Lemon Squeezy rejects any single usage-records POST whose quantity exceeds
1,000,000. One prod project (past3) had been failing 422 every day for
15 months: the report threw on provider failure, so apis.daily_usage and
projects.usage_last_reported never advanced, the window kept growing, and
every retry was guaranteed to fail again. Billing UI showed "0 requests".

Bookkeeping is now committed BEFORE any HTTP call. In one tx, ReportUsage
advances usage_last_reported (even on zero-usage days, which closes the
same poison-loop shape for quiet projects), inserts apis.daily_usage, and
queues N usage_report_submissions chunk rows. Both paid providers chunk
identically via splitUsageIntoChunks at 900k events. Chunks are then
drained in a loop; a per-row failure logs and marks the row 'failed',
never throws — so odd-jobs does not retry the whole job and no succeeded
chunk can double-submit. The next daily tick picks up any 'failed' /
'pending' rows via pendingUsageSubmissions.

Strong types enforce the invariants: ChunkQuantity newtype with smart
constructor rejects quantities outside (0, 900_000]; SubmissionOutcome
sum type collapses (status, submitted_at, last_error) so illegal
combinations are unrepresentable. Migration 0084 adds matching CHECK
constraints at the DB for defense in depth.

Other hardening:
- mark* calls wrapped in tryAny; on success-side DB blip we log
  "DOUBLE-SUBMIT RISK, manual reconcile required" with chunk_id,
  window_end, sub_id for on-call pivot.
- Stripe with missing customerId/orderId now throws so the chunk is
  marked 'failed' instead of silently marked 'submitted'.
- NoBillingProvider: one logAttention per tick + every pending chunk
  marked 'failed' as an audit signal, instead of silent 'submitted'.

Does not backfill past3's 15-month window; deploy-time reconciliation
is a follow-up.

feat(notify): dispatch team alerts for new log-pattern, rate-change and runtime-error issues

Three issue-creation paths were inserting into apis.issues without
calling sendAlertToChannels, so teams never learned about them unless
they happened to watch the inbox:

  processNewLogPatterns   -> LogPattern         (new ERROR/WARN pattern)
  detectLogPatternSpikes  -> LogPatternRateChange
  processProjectErrors    -> RuntimeException   (first-occurrence error)

Only detectErrorSpikes (sustained-rate anomaly) notified. A newly-deployed
regression that fires once and is never spike-anomalous would sit silent
in the inbox forever.

Wire all three through a new notifyIssue helper that:

  1. Atomically claims apis.issues.last_notified_at via a conditional
     UPDATE (added in migration 0085). Re-entry within the cooldown
     window is a no-op, which is the primary spam guard — without it,
     every hourly tick would re-alert every open issue.

  2. Gates on project.errorAlerts so customers keep their existing
     opt-out.

  3. Runs consumeNotificationToken (20/h/project cap). Overflow lands in
     apis.notification_digest_queue with the existing reason codes
     ('log_pattern', 'log_pattern_rate_change', 'runtime_exception'),
     flushed into one batched email per project by NotificationDigestJob.

Dedup windows chosen to match the rest of the system:
  - LogPattern: 6h (first-sighting matters more; shorter re-fire OK)
  - LogPatternRateChange: 24h (reuses Issues.rateChangeCooldownHours)
  - New RuntimeException: 24h

and PagerDuty payloads were already built in Pkg.Mail.

feat: expose monoscope as MCP server at /api/v1/mcp (#367)

* feat: expose monoscope as an MCP server at /api/v1/mcp

Adds a JSON-RPC endpoint that surfaces every ApiV1Routes operation as a
typed MCP tool. The registry is derived once from apiV1OpenApiSpec at
startup, so new endpoints become tools without touching MCP code; tool
calls are forwarded as synthetic WAI requests into a re-served inner
ApiV1Routes Application (no second auth pass, no handler duplication).

Tools cover initialize, tools/list, tools/call, and notifications/*.
Tool names are derived from path+method (e.g. monoscope_schema_get,
monoscope_monitors_monitor_id_get) since servant-openapi3 does not emit
operationIds for our spec; if operationIds are added later the registry
prefers them.

Tests cover registry shape, tools/list round-trip, initialize, tools/call
round-tripping monoscope_schema_get into Schema.telemetrySchema, and the
unknown-tool isError-not-JSON-RPC-error semantics.

* refactor(mcp): verb-first canonical tool names

Replaces auto-derived monoscope_<resource>_<id>_<action>_<method> names
with the verb-first snake_case convention every peer MCP server uses
(Sentry, Grafana, Datadog, Honeycomb): list_monitors, get_monitor,
mute_monitor, search_events, apply_dashboard, whoami, etc.

Names come from a canonical (method, path) override map in MCP.hs;
unmapped routes fall back to the path-derived name. The MCP endpoint
itself is excluded so agents cannot recurse into it.

Drops the redundant "monoscope_" prefix — MCP clients already namespace
tools by server name.

* feat(mcp): composite workflow tools + e2e HTTP coverage

Adds three Sentry/Grafana-style workflow tools alongside the OpenAPI-
derived REST tools:

- find_error_patterns — top established log patterns ranked by current
  hour count. Wraps getPatternsWithCurrentRates.
- search_events_nl — natural-language → KQL via runAgenticQuery; agent
  then calls search_events with the result.
- analyze_issue — fetches the issue and asks the LLM for a structured
  diagnosis (probable cause / signals / next steps).

Refactor: collapses ToolEntry + CompositeTool into one Tool record with
a Dispatch sum (ViaOpenApi | ViaComposite) — drops field-name prefixes,
single dispatcher path, single registry. allTools merges REST + composite
once at startup.

Derives ToJSON for LogPatternWithRate (snake_case via deriving-aeson) so
the composite tool returns it directly without a manual encoder.

Tests now cover the full dispatch chain: in-process registry/list/call
checks plus three e2e tests that POST through the real /api/v1/mcp HTTP
route with an API key and assert auth (401 without, 200 with) and tool
results (get_schema round-trips through to telemetrySchema).

fix(logging): tolerate writes to a shut-down bulk logger

The bulk logger's worker thread can transition to a closed state mid-
process (under heap pressure, or during withLogger teardown while other
threads are still emitting). Once that happens, every runLogT raises
AssertionFailed: 'attempt to write to a shut down logger'. That assertion
was escaping through every uncaught log site — supervise's own logExc,
kafkaService's runLogT, the periodic error-summary thread, Warp's
onException — and taking the process down with exit 137 (uncaught, not
kernel OOM).

write is swallowed. Single-point fix; every runLogT site is protected.

fix(replay): cap merge heap and stop per-save thundering herd

Threshold trigger fired on every save past 20 file_keys, so a busy session
queued dozens of duplicate MergeReplaySession jobs in seconds. Each merge
holds (existing merged.json.gz + N raw blobs + concat + gzip) — multiplied
by concurrent jobs that drove replicas past 8 GB on 2026-05-06 with R2
also rate-limiting the same merged.json.gz writes.

Trigger now fires only at exact multiples of the threshold (14, 28, 42…)
so each crossing enqueues at most one merge. Threshold lowered 20→14, and
each merge processes at most 25 file_keys per pass (heap ~80-150 MB
instead of ~330 MB+). When the snapshot exceeds the cap, the post-merge
path re-enqueues so backlogged sessions drain in chunks rather than
waiting 30 min for the periodic cron.

fix(replay): empty-string events no longer drop session ingestion

The hand-rolled JSON splitter introduced in 063556f0 had inconsistent
handling of opening `"` between callers: `skipJsonValue` left it in
the input, `skipBracketed` consumed it. The shared `skipJsonString`
unconditionally consumed one byte as the opener, so for empty strings
inside arrays/objects (`""`) it swallowed the closing `"` and ran past
the value. Decode failed, the message hit the silent
`replay:decode_error` counter, and the session ended up with zero
events — black player.

rrweb mutation events ship empty strings constantly (`data.text=""`,
removed `tagName`, empty `class`), so this affected ~every active
session post-deploy.

Fix: split into `skipStringBody` (assumes opening `"` already
consumed); `skipJsonValue` consumes `"` explicitly; `skipBracketed`
calls `skipStringBody` directly.

fix(schema): evict shard state + env kill switch to stop OOM crash loop

The in-process schema-learning shard state grew unbounded — evictLRU was
exported but never called, and knownTemplates was append-only. Every
distinct (project, keyHash) and every template hash a shard had ever seen
stayed pinned in memory, pushing prod past the 14 GB heap ceiling and
triggering the weekend crash loop (exit 251 / SIGSEGV).

Wire evictLRU into runSchemaFlusher so it runs each tick, cap
knownTemplates wholesale once it exceeds 50k (the set is just a dedup
short-circuit, re-populating is idempotent), and add an
ENABLE_SCHEMA_LEARNING env flag so the pipeline can be turned off without
a redeploy if the catalog misbehaves again.

fix(schema-learning): align endpoint hash + persist method/path on anomaly

Customers were getting Slack/Discord new-endpoint notifications with every
endpoint rendered as 'UNKNOWN /'. Root cause: 'extractObservation' hashed
the raw http.route/url.path, while 'processSpanToEntities' (which writes
apis.endpoints) hashed the canonical, SDK-normalised, template-matched
path. The schema-learning AKEndpoint target_hash therefore never matched
apis.endpoints.hash; the LEFT JOIN in 'getAnomaliesVM' returned NULL for
method/url_path; the renderer fell back to literal 'UNKNOWN' / '/'.

Three layered fixes:

1. Extract 'httpKeyOf' in ProcessMessage as the single source of truth for
   (method, host, urlPath, statusCode). Both 'processSpanToEntities' and
   'extractObservation' now share it, so their endpoint hashes are
   byte-identical. Threaded canonicalTemplates through extractObservation.

2. Persist method/host/url_path directly on apis.anomalies (migration 0092
   + new AnomalyInsertRow fields). 'buildAnomalyRows' reads them from the
   catalog Scope. 'getAnomaliesVM' COALESCEs anomaly row over the join, so
   notifications no longer depend on a successful endpoints-table match.

3. Guardrail in the new-endpoint notification path: if method+url_path are
   both unresolved, suppress the notification and logAttention instead of
   shipping a 'UNKNOWN /' label to customers.

feat(migrations): fail-fast on MigrationError instead of silently skipping

postgresql-simple-migration stops the runner at the first failure (e.g. a
checksum mismatch from an edited migration file) and returns
MigrationError. Previously we logged the result and continued booting, so
every later migration was silently skipped and the app started with a
half-applied schema — the failure only surfaced later as runtime SQL
errors. Caused the 2026-05-11 schema-flusher crash loop when an edit to
0091 blocked 0092 from running.

Refuse to start in that case so the operator sees the problem at boot,
not three handlers later.

fix(schema-learning): suppress endpoint anomalies for known/empty endpoints

Customers were getting Slack/Discord 'new endpoint' notifications for
endpoints that already existed in apis.endpoints — sometimes minutes after
the legacy discovery path had written them, sometimes for endpoints that
had been around for months. Root cause: 'diffAnomalies' decides isNew by
checking apis.schema_catalog (the new in-process catalog) alone. The
catalog was empty at this weekend's rollout and gets pruned by evictLRU,
so 'first seen by catalog' kept producing AKEndpoint anomalies regardless
of whether the endpoint was actually new to the project.

Also: many spans produce an endpoint hash with an empty url_path (when
http.route / url.path are both missing or normalisation strips them). The
notification path renders these as 'GET ' — useless.

Filter both classes out in Worker.flushDirty before insertAnomalies. The
existingEndpointHashes batched query cross-checks against apis.endpoints
in one round-trip per flush.

fix(schema-learning): only treat apis.endpoints rows >5min old as not-new

Previous filter unconditionally suppressed any AKEndpoint anomaly whose
target_hash matched apis.endpoints, including the row processSpanToEntities
had just inserted in the same batch — so notifications for genuinely new
endpoints would never fire. Schema-learning's flush runs ~60s after
ingestion; without a cutoff every new endpoint is already in apis.endpoints
by the time we check.

Restrict the dedupe query to endpoints created more than 5 minutes ago.
Endpoints discovered well before this flush cycle are 'not new' (suppress);
endpoints inserted in this batch are still new (notify).

Also correct misleading 'legacy discovery path' phrasing — apis.endpoints
is the canonical endpoint registry, not a legacy artifact; the
schema-learning catalog is structural learning layered on top.

fix(notifications): suppress on send side; let anomalies/issues land for UI

Previous patch filtered AKEndpoint anomalies out of the Worker so the
in-platform UI lost track of them entirely. Anomalies and the resulting
api_change issues are durable records the UI and downstream analytics
depend on — they must always be written. Only the Slack/Discord/email
*send* should be gated.

Restructure: Worker.flushDirty inserts all anomalies unconditionally.
processAPIChangeAnomalies creates the issue, then before dispatching
notifications, filters the candidate list against apis.endpoints (>5min
old → not new → skip) and unresolved method/path rows. Issues that were
filtered still exist; customers just don't get pinged.

Also start using apis.issues.last_notified_at: the old cooldown query
looked at created_at with a [-30min, -1min] window, which allowed
concurrent NewAnomaly jobs in the same 1-minute window to all squeeze
through. Switch to last_notified_at >= now-30min, and stamp it on issues
we just notified for, so subsequent sends in the cooldown window see the
correct state.

apis.issues.last_notified_at column already existed (used by error
subscriptions) — no migration needed.

feat(notifications): atomic per-issue claim for api_change rate limiting

The previous cooldown was project-coarse and read-then-write: SELECT
COUNT(...) WHERE last_notified_at >= now-30min, then send, then stamp.
Two concurrent NewAnomaly jobs both see count=0 and both proceed before
either UPDATE lands — every customer's spam complaint started here.

Replace with an atomic UPDATE...RETURNING that claims notifiable issues
in a single round-trip. Postgres serialises the row updates, so each
issue is claimed at most once per 30-min window. The RETURNING set is
exactly the issues we're permitted to dispatch — anything not returned
is either claimed by a concurrent job, still in cooldown, or has a
manual cooldown_until set (UI / LLM-enhancement override). Notification
fan-out runs only over the claimed set.

cooldown_until is now respected — admins / future logic can pin a
per-issue silence window without changing this code.
chore: drop unused Effectful.Reader.Static qualified import

fix(background-jobs): cap UPDATE lock + statement time to prevent pool exhaustion

Wrap the otel_logs_and_spans enrichment UPDATE in an explicit transaction
with SET LOCAL lock_timeout='30s' and statement_timeout='5min'. A runaway
2-hour UPDATE held chunk locks, queued TimescaleDB compression behind an
AccessExclusiveLock, cascaded 48 blocked connections, exhausted PgBouncer,
and caused a 1-hour 502 outage. Now the UPDATE aborts cleanly instead.
feat(issues): render proper not-found page for missing issue hashes

fix(schema): hard cap shard entries on hot path to prevent OOM between evictions

mergeGroup now drops new keys once a shard exceeds maxEntriesPerShard (10k),
preventing unbounded growth in the 60s windows between evictLRU ticks.
Lowered maxKeysPerProject default from 5000→500 so the bounded steady-state
(500 keys × 4 shards × N projects × ~10KB/entry) stays well under the 16 GB
container limit even with hundreds of active projects.

refactor(queue,otlp): tighten queue/otlp pipeline logging and time tracking

- Replace ad-hoc liftIO getCurrentTime + manual diff with Log.timeAction in
  processBatchPipeline and processList; drop redundant local bindings.
- Collapse per-call runLogT scaffolding in kafkaService into a single
  LogT/localData context so client_id/group_id/topic ride along automatically.
- Group kafka poll results by topic before dispatch so multi-topic polls get
  the right ce-type and attributes per batch.
- Move kafkaProducerProps under getOrInitKafkaProducer (only caller).
- publishToDeadLetterQueue now logs publish failures instead of silently
  discarding them; threads appLogger through pubsub/kafka callers.
- Simplify Start.startApp tracer bracket.

fix(otelcol): coerce numeric level attrs to string for severity_text

OTTL set(severity_text, ...) requires a string; clients emitting numeric
level (pino/syslog) made transform/tier1 spam 'expects string but got
float64' warnings and skip severity_text entirely. Wrap each lookup in
String() so both string and numeric levels assign cleanly.

refactor(billing): split data size per bucket and flag no-metrics cycles

Pair each count column in the daily-usage breakdown with its byte
subtitle (events bytes under events, metrics bytes under metrics) and
render an inline notice when the cycle has no metric ingestion. Widens
the settings section container so the breakdown table breathes.

fix(tests): drive schema-learning flush in drainExtractionWorker

Anomaly creation moved off DB triggers (dropped in 0090) onto
SchemaLearning.Worker.flushDirty, which prod runs from
runSchemaFlusherFiber on a timer. Tests never ticked that fiber, so
processMessagesAndBackgroundJobs never enqueued any NewAnomaly jobs and
the AnomaliesSpec / ApiCatalogSpec assertions about api_change issues
all failed (8 in AnomaliesSpec, 3 in ApiCatalogSpec).

Drive flushDirty after the drain-flush pass so anomalies + jobs land
before runAllBackgroundJobs.

fix(error_patterns): gate toastable-column refresh on regression only

ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE was unconditionally re-assigning message,
error_data, and parent_hash from EXCLUDED on every occurrence.
PostgreSQL writes a fresh TOAST datum on each such SET even when
the value is byte-identical, so a hot error pattern firing
thousands of times per hour bloated apis.error_patterns' pg_toast
to 157 GB (vs 400 MB live data, 7k rows).

Since hash is content-derived, those fields don't change across
occurrences; only refresh them on the resolved -> regressed
transition where new context is legitimately useful.

feat(drain): gate hashes UPDATEs by env flag and 2h age cutoff

Adds ENABLE_HASH_UPDATES kill switch and HASH_UPDATE_MAX_AGE_SECS
(default 7200s) so UPDATE-1 (eager hash merge) and UPDATE-2 (drain pat:*
tag append) never touch already-compressed chunks of
otel_logs_and_spans, which was forcing chunk decompression.

fix(log-explorer): opaque badge-neutral + reveal clipped cell on hover

badge-neutral was rendering on near-transparent fillWeaker (alpha 0.02/0.03),
so service-column text bled through neighboring columns. Switch to bgAlternate
for a fully opaque background, and clip non-summary cells at rest while
revealing them on hover (overflow-visible + z-30) so the full badge floats
above the next column and stays readable.

fix(schema-learning): scrub NUL bytes + isolate flush failures to stop heap OOM

Schema-catalog jsonb writes (scope/valuesDelta/counts) occasionally carried
\NUL bytes from user payloads, tripping SQLSTATE 22P05. The exception escaped
flushDirty, killed the per-shard flusher fiber, and the dirty set then grew
unboundedly until the RTS hit the 14 GB heap ceiling (exit 251, ~6-min
restart loop in prod).

- SchemaCatalog: scrubNulValue rewrites NUL → U+FFFD in jsonb values pre-insert
- BackgroundJobs: tryAny around flushDirty so one bad batch can't kill the fiber
- Worker: document the invariant that flushOne must catch its own exceptions

feat(log-patterns): persist is_error and surface it in alerts + UI

Single source of truth for "this pattern is from error-bearing events" —
set at drain extraction from Telemetry.isErrorRecord (level/severity/status),
OR-merged on upsert so a pattern that ever fires as an error stays flagged.
Slack/Discord/email/PagerDuty alert titles branch on it (🚨 error · ⚠️ warn
· 🔍 log) and the patterns UI shows a red "error" badge. Slack alert also
gains the sample-message block for parity with Discord/email.

feat(i18n): YAML-driven translations + language switcher (#397)

Per-language strings live in static/i18n/<code>.yaml. Two languages ship
today (en, es). Adding a third only needs a new YAML file, a constructor
in 'Language', and the matching cases in 'parseLanguage'/'languageCode'.

- New 'Web.I18n' module: 'Language' (En, Es), 't lang key' lookup,
  cookie helpers ('languageFromCookies', 'languageSetCookieBS').
  YAML is embedded into the binary at compile time via 'file-embed' so
  the runtime stays pure and decode errors fail the build.
- 'Projects.Session' gains a 'lang :: Language' field; the value is read
  from the 'lang' cookie at session-build time alongside theme/isSidebarClosed.
- 'GET /set_language/<code>?redirect_to=…' persists the cookie (Max-Age 1yr)
  and bounces the user back.
- Sidebar nav items and the user-menu dropdown render via 't sess.lang';
  the dropdown also shows the EN/ES switcher (rewrites href to current path
  on click so users don't get bounced to /).
- Tests: 'testSessionHeader' / 'refreshSession' pass a default language
  through the new 'sessionByID' parameter.

Missing keys fall through to the raw key, so typos surface as visible
'nav.dashboards' strings in the UI rather than blanks.

schema-learning: efficiency pass to unblock re-enabling in prod

Background: the in-process schema-learning pipeline has been disabled in
prod (ENABLE_SCHEMA_LEARNING=False) since the OOM incidents earlier this
year. An audit surfaced four hot-path inefficiencies, all of which now
have load-bearing tests.

Changes:

1. Per-entry field cap. mergeFullWalk now takes a maxFieldsPerEntry from
   DecisionPolicy; new paths past the cap are dropped silently while
   existing paths still update. New config knob
   schemaCatalogMaxFieldsPerEntry (default 2000) plumbed through
   EnvConfig → BackgroundJobs.processEagerBatch.

2. Byte budget + between-tick eviction. SchemaShardState now tracks a
   running bytesEstimate incremented per merge. observeSpans triggers
   evictLRU inline whenever the estimate exceeds the (previously dead)
   schemaCatalogMaxBytesPerShard config. evictLRU does a second pass that
   drops globally-oldest entries until the byte budget is met. This is
   what protects against the 60-second windows of unbounded growth that
   triggered the past OOMs.

3. Lazy walk thunk (sample-before-extract). ObservationInput.walk is now
   () -> [...] instead of a strict list. extractObservation builds the
   thunk eagerly but the expensive valueToFields + per-leaf regex sweep
   only runs when Hot.mergeGroup forces it under the sample gate. At the
   default learnSampleEveryN=200, ~99% of spans bump-only and never pay
   the walk cost.

4. In-shard prior snapshot + skip-unchanged summary writes. Worker now
   keeps a flushedEntries snapshot per shard and uses it for anomaly diff
   priors instead of issuing a getByKeysBatch every flush; only cold-start
   keys (never persisted in-process) fall through to the DB. Summary
   upserts also compare a content hash against flushedSummaryHashes; docs
   that didn't change are skipped entirely. The 30s freshness gate is
   kept as a multi-replica safeguard.

Tests: new SchemaLearningPerfSpec pins each invariant (shard byte budget,
per-entry field cap, summary skip-on-unchanged, in-memory anomaly prior,
lazy walk laziness). Existing FacetsSpec and SchemaLearningSpec stay
green. mkObs in SchemaLearningSpec updated for the lazy walk signature.

schema-learning: unblock summary upsert on NUL-tainted observed values

Root cause of the 2026-05-30 OOM crash loop on monoscope-prod-eu: span
attributes from kubernetes events contained literal NUL bytes, which
aeson serialised into the SummaryDoc as the valid JSON escape \\u0000.
PG jsonb rejects that with 22P05 ("unsupported Unicode escape sequence"),
so every batched unnest insert into apis.schema_summary failed wholesale
— one rogue project poisoned every project that flushed alongside it.
With summary writes permanently failing, flushedSummaryHashes never
converged, every tick re-serialised the same docs, and the process
OOM'd at the 14 GB GHC heap cap in ~28 min, looping until manually
disabled.

    scrubNulValue helper (the same one upsertCatalogRows already used).
  * On batch failure it retries per-row so one hostile project can't
    block the rest.

    ProcessMessage.stripNulBytes into Utils as the single source.

ingestion: TF-strict commit, per-partition offsets, row-level bisection (#402)

* ingestion: TF-strict commit, per-partition offsets, row-level bisection

The 2026-06-01 TimescaleDB outage exposed several ways the consumer
advances Kafka offsets past failed batches, losing hours of customer
data. Commit semantics, the dual-write asymmetry, and the fire-and-forget
DLQ all combined to step over any failure that wasn't a hard exception.

- kafkaService now commits per (topic, partition) via
  commitPartitionsOffsets. Only groups whose batch succeeded -- or whose
  poison content was successfully DLQ'd -- contribute offsets. Failed
  groups leave their partitions uncommitted; lag growth becomes the
  outage signal. DLQ is no longer subscribed by the live loop.
- pubsubService mirrors: poison -> DLQ-then-ack; transient -> no ack.
- publishToDeadLetterQueue returns Either Text () so the caller can gate
  commit on DLQ success.
- bulkInsertOtelLogsAndSpans bisects on non-transient Hasql failures,
  isolating a single poison row in O(log N) attempts so a bad row no
  longer wedges the partition.
- bulkInsertOtelLogsAndSpansTF requires TF success to return normally;
  PG-only failure is logged via PG_WRITE_FAILED_TF_OK and tolerated (PG
  is being phased out).
- New Pkg/IngestError classifier replaces the brittle string-match
  isUnrecoverableError. Unknown errors default to PoisonBatch
  (DLQ-actionable) rather than TransientInfra (silent stall).

refactor(LogQueries): collapse wrappers onto jsonb_build_array(sub.*) (#423)

* refactor(LogQueries): wrap row-extraction with jsonb_build_array

executeArbitraryQuery previously wrapped each row with
SELECT (SELECT json_agg(x.value ORDER BY x.ordinality)::jsonb
        FROM json_each(row_to_json(sub.*)) WITH ORDINALITY AS x) FROM (...) sub
to coerce arbitrary rows into a single jsonb-array column for hasql to decode
into Vector AE.Value.

That wrapper is portable to Postgres only. TimeFusion (DataFusion-backed)
ships neither json_each, row_to_json, WITH ORDINALITY, nor row-correlated
lateral UDTFs — the wrapper made TF unable to serve log-explorer queries
through this path. The wrapper also tripped PostgreSQL's own JSON parser on
TEXT columns containing NULL bytes or lone surrogates (see prior comment at
the RawSessionRow site), forcing typed-decoder workarounds.

Replaced with the equivalent SQL:
  SELECT jsonb_build_array(c1,...,cN) FROM (<inner>) sub(c1,...,cN)

This works natively on both backends:
  - Postgres: jsonb_build_array(VARIADIC any) -> jsonb is built-in.
  - TimeFusion: json_build_array UDF now exposes a jsonb_build_array alias.

executeArbitraryQuery gains a column-count parameter; the two callers
(selectLogTable, fetchEventExamples) already know it via
queryComponents.toColNames / colsNoAsClause cols. Derived-column aliases
sub(c1,...,cN) decouple the wrapper from the inner SELECT's expression shapes
so we never have to introspect those.

Side effect: the JSON-parser hazard documented near RawSessionRow is also
gone for the Postgres path, since jsonb_build_array builds JSON from typed
values instead of re-parsing a Postgres-side text serialization.

executeSecuredQuery (Dashboards / AI raw-SQL path) is left on the legacy
wrapper for now — its callers don't have column-count info and never worked
against TimeFusion anyway.

Helper exposed as Pkg.Parser.wrapForRowExtraction for future callers that
want to wrap their own SQL.

fix(LogQueries): PG-side jsonb_build_array(record) overload + inline projection wrap

PR #423's `SELECT jsonb_build_array(sub.*) FROM (...) sub` works on TF
(WildcardFnArgExpander analyzer rule) but breaks on PG: `sub.*` inside
a function call passes the row as a single composite, yielding a
1-element jsonb array per row. Root cause of the "index out of bounds
(7,1)" failures across log explorer, gRPC sessions aggregation, CLI
events search, and trace-tree expansion.

Internal callers (selectLogTable, selectChildSpansAndLogs,
fetchEventExamples) know their projection lists — they now inline
`SELECT jsonb_build_array(<bare-cols>) FROM ...` directly. Same wire
shape on both backends, no analyzer-rule dependency, ~0.22ms / 200-row
page measured. executeArbitraryQuery deleted.

executeSecuredQuery (Dashboards widgets, Pkg.AI raw SQL — opaque
projection, must reach TF) keeps the `sub.*` wrapper. Migration 0099
adds a PL/pgSQL `jsonb_build_array(record)` overload so PG dispatches
the same shape; STABLE because row_to_json honors STABLE per-column
output functions (e.g. timestamptz's TimeZone GUC).

Also: splitTrailingAlias is case-insensitive (aggregations emit
uppercase AS; jsonb_build_array args reject any AS); the duplicate
`stripAlias` in applySectionToComponent collapses onto it.

fix(LogQueries): cast jsonb_build_array to text so TF reads work; simplify timestampLogFmt

TimeFusion's `jsonb_build_array` returns `Utf8View` (PG wire OID 25 = text),
not jsonb (OID 3802) — hasql's jsonb decoder rejects the result whenever
selectLogTable / fetchEventExamples / executeSecuredQuery route through
the TF read path (Hasql.withHasqlTimefusion). On every backend we now emit
`SELECT jsonb_build_array(...)::text FROM ...` and decode `[Text]` +
`AE.eitherDecodeStrict` in Haskell. Same wire shape both sides, no TF
type-coercion required.

Also simplify timestampLogFmt: the old multi-line CASE existed because
TF didn't have proper to_char/timestamp-with-Z support. It does now, so
swap the whole block for one `to_char(... 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS.US"Z"')`
call — works identically on PG and TF.

Tests updated to the new shape; doctests still pass.

revert(LogQueries): drop ::text cast — TF now returns jsonb over the wire

Earlier commit 0078dc54 cast jsonb_build_array(...)::text everywhere and
decoded as [Text] + parse, because TF's jsonb_build_array used to return
Utf8View (PG wire OID 25) which hasql's jsonb decoder rejected. TimeFusion
now ships proper jsonb wire-type support, so the cast and the Text-decode

The DLQ-replay consumer (and primary consumer) inherited librdkafka's
default per-partition/total fetch ceilings, which are below the 64 MiB
broker/producer message cap. Re-stamped DLQ records and large legit OTLP
batches near that cap were returned truncated, so the valid protobuf
failed to decode as "Unknown wire type 6/7" and write-failure replays
re-DLQ'd them forever. Set fetch.message.max.bytes/fetch.max.bytes/
receive.message.max.bytes above the cap so a full message fits in one
fetch.

dlq: publish raw message bytes, not JSON-wrapped binary

publishToDeadLetterQueue routed payloads through publishJSONToKafka, which
JSON-string-encodes its input (BC.unpack then AE.encode). For binary OTLP
protobuf that quotes and escapes the bytes into an undecodable blob: the
replay consumer fails to protobuf-decode it ("Unknown wire type 6/7"),
re-DLQs it, and re-escapes it on every pass, so the payload balloons (8+
MiB) and cycles forever — the tf-failed carousel that filled the DLQ.

Split publishJSONToKafka into a publishRawToKafka core (verbatim bytes) plus
a thin JSON wrapper; the DLQ now publishes the original bytes via
dlqRecordValue so the replay consumer decodes them unchanged. Reverts the
earlier consumer fetch-size change (a20ac44c), which addressed a misdiagnosed
truncation-on-consume cause and was not the bug.

identical to the original proto and that the old JSON-wrap path mangles it.

CONSUMER_ONLY=True runs the queue consumers (Kafka/PubSub) and the
extraction / schema-learning pipeline — which flushes the spans the
instance ingested and writes learnt derivations back to those rows — but
skips Warp, gRPC OTLP, odd-jobs and the global periodic timers. Lets you

* fix: concurrent bounded shutdown so Ctrl-C/SIGTERM actually exits

runServer ended in async's waitAnyCancel, whose `mapM_ cancel` cancels
fibers sequentially and blocks on each one's death before signalling the
next. One slow-to-die fiber (Warp's graceful drain, a wedged librdkafka
poll) kept every later fiber alive — so Ctrl-C left the kafka workers
retrying dead-DB writes and emitting consumer metrics instead of exiting.

Replace with awaitShutdown: install SIGINT+SIGTERM handlers, race a signal
against any fiber exiting, then cancelAllConcurrently — mapConcurrently_
cancel under a 15s deadline. Teardown is now bounded by the slowest single
fiber, not the sum, and a wedged fiber can't hang the process. Catching
SIGTERM also lets docker stop / k8s drain gracefully instead of SIGKILL.

cancelAllConcurrently is exported for the regression test in ServerSpec.

fix(queue): self-heal DLQ commit-starvation via reseek on no-ack (#443)

* fix(queue): self-heal DLQ commit-starvation via reseek on no-ack

A consumer chunk that returns no acks (transient write/DLQ-publish
failure → routeBatchOutcome []) does not advance the commit base, but
the poll position has already moved past it. librdkafka never redelivers
uncommitted offsets in-session, so the base pins forever while the
consumer forward-processes to log-end and goes idle — the 2026-06-25
apitoolkit_eu_dlq wedge (~7.6M lag, committed offsets frozen).

Fix: on no-ack, the worker records the chunk's lowest offset in reseekVar;
the poll thread (which owns all Kafka ops) seeks each such partition back
to that offset and resets its tracker so the un-acked chunk is redelivered
and retried once the failure clears. Seeks backward only (never past the
committed base) so it can never skip — worst case redelivers
already-processed offsets, which is idempotent downstream.

Regression test in KafkaConsumerSpec drives a chunk that no-acks on first
processing then acks: without the fix the base pins and the watermark
never recovers (drive times out); with it the reseek redelivers and the
commit advances. Adds SeekPartitions to the in-memory broker mock.

* fix(queue): address reseek review — prune reseekVar on rebalance + test rigor

- Prune reseekVar to the live partition set in the committer (alongside
  tracker/committed). Without it, a partition that stalled (reseek recorded)
  then got revoked would make the poll thread seek a partition this consumer
  no longer owns and re-seed a stale tracker entry the prune can never reach.
- Tracker reset on reseek uses the left-biased Map union
  (Map.map (`PartProgress` mempty) reseeks <> tk) instead of folding a toList.
- Test: assert the retry actually fired (attemptVar >= 2), so removing the
  no-ack guard can't make the test pass trivially.
- Test mock: key the broker cursor by (topic, partition) so same-topic

fix(ingest): deterministic content-derived row id so DLQ replay is idempotent (#445)

* fix(ingest): deterministic content-derived row id so DLQ replay is idempotent

mintOtelLogIds assigned a fresh random UUID v4 per row, so reprocessing a
dead-letter message wrote a brand-new row every time — the source of the
06-19 duplicate pile-up (and the reseek self-heal, which redelivers chunks,
makes reprocessing more frequent). TF already dedups on (id, timestamp)
(flush-time dedup_batches + today-partition sweep + read-side row_number
rewrite), but random ids defeated it.

Make `id` content-derived (UUID v5): spans key on the OTel-unique
(project_id, trace_id, span_id) — matching TF's "same span id collapses
retries" intent regardless of attribute drift; logs (no span_id) key on
stable content (project_id, body, name, severity, attributes, resource).
Excludes timestamp (the other dedup key, so co-content/different-time events
stay distinct) and the parse-time fallback fields (observed_timestamp/
start_time → currentTime) which aren't stable across reprocessing. So
re-parsing the same payload re-derives the same id and TF collapses the dup.

mintOtelLogIds becomes pure; UUIDEff drops out of the ingest path
(Telemetry.insertSystemLog + OtlpServer) — those used it solely for minting.
Unit test asserts determinism, span-retry collapse, span/content distinctness,
timestamp-exclusion, and no over-collapse across differing resource.

* fix(log-explorer): page earlier/load-more cursor from the oldest loaded row

The cursor for 'show earlier events' and load-more was derived from
spanListTree[length-1]. spanListTree is the flattened trace tree: each
trace pushes its root first then DFS-appends child spans (which always
start >= their parent), and traces sort newest-start-first. So the last
array element is a newer child leaf of the oldest trace, not the oldest
row. The cursor came out newer than the last visible row (e.g. visible
16:54:45 but cursor 16:55:02), so 'earlier' re-fetched rows already shown.

* fix(log-explorer): exact-timestamp random-access lookup, not a ±1s window

Single-row item detail lookups (web log-item detail + the CLI/API
/events/{id}/time/{ts} path, both via lookupOtelRecord) matched
`timestamp BETWEEN ts-1s AND ts+1s AND id = ?`. The caller always holds
the exact stored timestamp (it comes from a prior query result), so match
`timestamp = ts` instead: both PG and TF store microsecond precision,
which round-trips losslessly through the UTCTime↔Hasql encoder, and exact
equality lets the planner hit the (timestamp, id) ordering rather than
scanning a window. Regression test asserts an off-by-1s timestamp no
longer resolves the row on either the TF or PG read path.

* fix(log-explorer): propagate the red error badge from error logs and missing-span parents

The trace waterfall lights a parent row's [+N] badge red via childErrors,
but error LOGS never contributed: the worker hardcoded hasErrors=false for
kind=log, and the trace-view `errors` column only reflected structured
error payloads (which severity-only error logs lack). So an error log — or
an orphan error log nested under a synthetic "missing span" parent — left
its parent's badge un-reddened.

- log-worker-functions: derive a log's error-ness from the errors flag and
  severity (text or OTel number >=17); spans unchanged. Now error logs and
  their (possibly synthetic) parents propagate childErrors.
- defaultSelectSqlQuery: fold log severity into the `errors` projection
  (mirrors LogQueries.is_error) so the signal actually reaches the client.

Vitest covers direct + synthetic-parent propagation and the info-log
non-regression; an integration test asserts the errors column is set for
ERROR-severity logs.

* perf(prometheus): fan-out dispatcher + SKIP LOCKED claim for multi-node scaling

The per-minute tick scraped every due target sequentially in one job on one
pod — at hundreds/thousands of targets the tick wall-time exceeds the interval,
one hung endpoint stalls the batch, and two pods running it would double-scrape.

Rework into a distributed-queue model (leans on odd-jobs, which already gives a
cross-pod worker pool + retries):

- claimDueConfigs: atomic `UPDATE ... WHERE id IN (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP
  LOCKED LIMIT n) RETURNING ...`. Safe to run on every node — each due row is
  leased to exactly one caller, and the same statement bumps last_scraped_at so
  the next tick (any node) won't re-pick it before its interval. Oldest-first so
  a backlog drains fairly.
- PrometheusScrapeTick is now a cheap dispatcher: claim + fan out one
  PrometheusScrapeOne job per target. Workers across all pods drain those, so
  throughput scales horizontally with the fleet instead of a single loop.
- PrometheusScrapeOne worker: hard per-scrape HTTP response timeout (10s) via a
  manager-level managerResponseTimeout, so a dead endpoint can't wedge a worker;
  failures are caught (the lease handles back-off, no retry storm).

fix(charts): don't advance query-cache watermark on failed delta fetch (#455)

Time-series chart widgets could render permanent holes: in the partial-hit
path, a delta fetch that failed (timeout / TF planning error / dropped conn,
swallowed into an empty MetricsData by withChartSpan) still advanced cached_to
to the request end. That orphaned the [cachedTo, reqTo] window forever, since
every later delta starts from the advanced watermark — so short ranges rendered
near-empty while wider ranges (a separate bin_interval cache entry) looked fine.

Gate updateCache on `isNothing deltaData.error` in both the PartialHit and
CacheMiss branches, so the watermark never advances past data we actually
fetched. On a transient failure the next poll re-fetches [cachedTo, now] and
backfills the gap.

Regression tests in QueryCacheSpec: failed delta doesn't advance cached_to and
still serves the cached rows; a successful-but-empty delta still advances.

Bound dead-socket hangs on all PG/TF pools: connect_timeout + tcp_user_timeout

2026-07-04 incident: after TimeFusion OOM kills, one kafka consumer member
sat in a single uninterruptible libpq call for 40+ minutes (frozen
inflight_bytes, zero commits), wedging its partitions while the rest of the
group drained. Keepalives were already configured but cover only the
idle-peer case; two hangs escape them:

- connection establishment had no bound (hasql-pool's acquisitionTimeout
  only bounds slot-wait, not libpq connect) -> connect_timeout=5
- writes with unacked data in the send queue suppress keepalive probes and
  ride the ~15-25min kernel retransmit ceiling -> tcp_user_timeout=30000
  (Linux-only; libpq ignores it elsewhere)

The kernel now surfaces dead sockets as connection errors, which the
existing transient-retry/DLQ classification already routes correctly.
A client-side wall-clock bound for a live-but-unresponsive peer is NOT
included: hasql blocks in a safe (non-interruptible) FFI call and
hasql-pool 1.4.2 returns mid-protocol connections to the pool on async
exception, so a timeout wrapper needs detach-and-poison semantics — split
out as follow-up work.

fix(ingest): per-engine SELECT casts for unnest insert (restore Postgres writes)

The column-oriented unnest insert sent id + JSON columns as text[] and relied on
text→uuid/jsonb coercion. That works on TimeFusion (VariantInsertRewriter), but
PostgreSQL/TimescaleDB has NO text→uuid or text→jsonb assignment cast, so the
SELECT threw "column is of type jsonb but expression is of type text" — failing
the PRIMARY (PG) leg of every dual-write → all ingestion DLQ'd (prod outage).

Fix: bulkInsertOtelLogsAndSpans takes a `usePgTypes` Bool; the statement builder
casts id `::uuid` and JSON columns `::jsonb` in the SELECT when True (Postgres),
and leaves them bare text when False (TimeFusion coerces to Variant). Array bind
params are identical for both engines; only these columns' SELECT projection
differs. Dual-write passes True for the pg leg, False for the tf leg.

Verified: exact PG statement (::uuid/::jsonb + string_to_array unnest) lands rows
on a Timescale temp table; TF text→Variant path proven by the tf-repo e2e.
Follow-up: teach TF pgwire the jsonb/uuid array OIDs so both legs can send native
types and the usePgTypes bool goes away.

insertAndHandOff / insertSystemLog, sourced from the new
`timefusionUsesPgTypes` config field (default False = real TF).

The test suite points its "timefusion" leg at a plain Postgres, which (like
the pg leg) has no text→uuid/jsonb coercion, so TestUtils sets the flag True
when no real TF is wired (isNothing tfPgUrl). Fixes the TimefusionWriteFailure

fix(log-explorer): honor requested columns that alias-collide with defaults

getProcessedColumns deduped requested projection columns by SQL expression, so
requesting "name" (expr `name`) was dropped as a duplicate of the default
`name as span_name`. But that default's output alias is `span_name`
(hidden-by-default), so curateCols then hid it and the requested column vanished
— e.g. `?cols=id,timestamp,name,duration` returned everything except name.

Dedup by output alias instead: a requested column is a true duplicate only when
its alias already appears in the defaults; one resolving to the same DB expr
under a different default alias is still projected under the requested alias.

perf(ingest): cut hot-table lock contention on otel_logs_and_spans

Root cause of the 2026-07-06 wedge: every hot span row is rewritten 5–9×
after insert by three concurrent writers over the same recent rows —
UPDATE-1 (hash merge, 4 shards), UPDATE-2 (pat:* tag append), and the
session-backfill sweep — with inconsistent row-lock acquisition order.
Result: lock-order deadlocks (40P01, 188 counted) + lock_timeout pileups
(55P03), and a full table wedge whenever one such txn orphaned idle.

P1 — consistent lock ordering (kills the 40P01 class):
- UPDATE-2 now orders its unnest source by (span_id, trace_id), matching
  UPDATE-1, so both hash writers lock rows in the same order.
- session-backfill locks its targets via `ORDER BY (span_id, trace_id)
  FOR UPDATE OF o` before updating — same order as UPDATE-1/2.

P2 — take the sweep off the write-hot edge:
- session-backfill window lags to 2–17 min old (was 0–15 min), so it no
  longer contends with the fresh rows UPDATE-1/2 and the INSERTs are
  hammering. The ingest cache already stamps the common case; cross-batch
  gaps are settled well within 2 min, so the lag costs nothing.

Test: TraceSessionPropagationSpec aged into the window + a lag guard
asserting a <2 min span is skipped by the sweep.

test(session-backfill): verify propagation through the lagged 2–17 min window

Base the backfill spec's timestamps on the DB clock (not the host) so the
sweep's NOW()-relative window is exercised deterministically under docker
clock skew. Drops the fresh-span "lag guard" assertion: the ingest cache
already back-stamps recently-buffered spans when the session source arrives,
so a fresh span never reaches the DB sweep unstamped — the exclusion isn't
observable via session values, only the aged-row propagation is.

fix(dlq): stop committing past skipped not-yet-due replay records

but the poll position moved past them (librdkafka never redelivers in-session)

made the skip durable. Under sustained write-leg failure (TF down 7h on

fix(kql): generate valid Postgres jsonpath for wildcard-array predicates

KQL predicates on wildcard-array subjects (foo[*].bar) were rendered by
splicing the KQL operator token verbatim into the jsonpath filter, so every
non-comparison operator produced invalid jsonpath that Postgres/TimeFusion
reject: `@ is null`, `@ IN [...]`, `@ HAS/CONTAINS/STARTSWITH/ENDSWITH "x"`,
`@ now()`, `@ ago(...)`, and the NOT_ variants.

Replace the string-splicing jsonPathQuery with a typed target IR (Jsonpath /
JPred / JCmpOp / JLit) plus:
- lowerPred :: Text -> Subject -> Values -> Either LowerErr Jsonpath, a total
  translation that maps each KQL operator to valid jsonpath (in -> ||-eq chain,
  has/contains/startswith/endswith -> escaped like_regex, = null -> == null),
- renderJsonpath, total by construction so it can only emit valid jsonpath,
  single-quoted with ''-escaping (not $$ dollar-quoting a value could break).

Negation of a wildcard predicate now wraps the whole existence test
(NOT jsonb_path_exists(...)) instead of pushing ! into the $[*] ? (...) filter,
which had the wrong quantifier (matched rows where *some* element failed).

now()/ago() have no jsonpath form; resolveWildcardTimes resolves them to a
concrete ISO-8601 instant at query-build time (fresh each execution) so they
lower to a jsonpath .datetime() comparison. Non-wildcard comparisons are
untouched and still render NOW()/INTERVAL.

Consolidate the duplicated escapeRegex into Pkg.DeriveUtils.

fix(replay): serialize session merges to stop replica OOM crash-loop

A single high-rate replay session accumulated ~24 concurrent
MergeReplaySession jobs, each decompressing a 528 MB merged.json.gz into
multi-GB heap; together they exhausted memory and pegged CPU on every app
replica, which then failed health checks and were reaped — rolling 502s
(2026-07-13 incident).

Add a per-session merge lease (merge_started_at) so at most one worker
merges a given session at a time; duplicate/queued jobs claim-and-skip.
Stale leases (>15 min, from a worker that died mid-merge) are reclaimable.

Also adds a CPU+memory benchmark of the merge hot path (test/bench) that
reproduces the blowup against real session data and compares an O(n)
bounded-shard candidate (~6x faster, ~26x less allocation).

perf(replay): bounded shards + progressive lazy-loading player

Layer B of the replay-merge overhaul (Layer A serialized merges via a
per-session lease). Replaces the single, unboundedly-growing merged.json.gz
with append-only, byte-bounded shards (<sid>/shard-<idx>-<firstTs>.json.gz):

- mergeOneSession seals ≤12 MiB shards one at a time and never re-reads prior
  shards, so a growing session is O(n) with flat per-merge heap instead of the
  O(n²) monolith re-decompress+recompress that OOM'd replicas. The shard key
  encodes index + first-event timestamp so the read/manifest path can order
  shards and answer "which shard covers time T" from a bucket listing alone.
- New manifest (replay_session/<sid>/manifest) + shard-fetch
  (replay_session/<sid>/shard?key=) endpoints. The events endpoint keeps
  working (now reads legacy monolith + shards + unmerged tail).
- Player (session-replay.ts) fetches the manifest, plays shard 1 immediately,
  then streams the rest via rrweb addEvent — never downloading the whole
  session up front, and the server never stitches it into one giant response.
  Share links keep the full-events fallback.

Tests: MinIO round-trip proving batches → ordered shards → manifest →
in-order read; vitest coverage of the progressive loader (manifest fetch,
shard-1 playback, ordered streaming, error + share paths).

fix(session-backfill): scope per-project + dual-write to TimeFusion

The session/user backfill sweep ran one cross-tenant UPDATE with no
project_id filter and only against Postgres:

- No project_id defeated every (project_id, ...) index, forcing
  cross-tenant seq scans + a row-locking join that blew past the 2min
  statement_timeout (57014).

  straggler rows stayed un-enriched in the store we're migrating to.

Reshape into the same TF-compatible `UPDATE ... FROM` shape UPDATE-1/2
use and run it through the existing dualExecPgTf primitive:

- Per-project scoping: mandatory for TF (rejects UPDATE without a
  project_id filter) and lets the partial session/user indexes drive
  the PG plan instead of a full scan.
- One SQL serves both engines (TF executes it via its Delta
  MergeBuilder) — advisory lock + FOR UPDATE dropped (PG-only, rejected
  by TF); deadlocks handled by dualExecPgTf's retryOnDeadlock, same as
  the sibling hash-writers.
- Window bounds computed via the Time effect (testable) instead of DB
  NOW(), keeping the documented 2-17min lag.

unconditionally, so projects with TimeFusion reads enabled saw empty
event counts, last-seen, and activity charts.

TimeFusion is telemetry-only and can't serve apis.* tables, so the

fix(otlp): never ack a payload that carried telemetry but converted to zero rows

2026-07-27: ~200k rows across 10 tenants disappeared during a 9-minute window
with no failure signal anywhere. Spans were produced to Kafka and consumed at
a normal rate, offsets were committed, and not one message reached
otlp_deadletter / -retry-60s / -retry-600s / -parking. monoscope logged
"outcome": "ok" for every batch.

TimeFusion was cleared: a new SIGKILL suite (timefusion tests/kill_recovery.rs)
proves acked writes survive kill -9 under flush, memory pressure, multi-tenant
sharding and concurrency, and the DV-merge append-rebase does not drop
concurrent appends. Prod logs show zero TF_WRITE_FAILED and zero retries in
01:33-01:46 — the writes were never attempted.

processBatchPipeline treated "converted to zero rows" as success. But zero rows
is ambiguous: it is also what happens when a payload's project never resolves.
projectIdsByProjectApiKeys returns a clean Nothing for an unresolvable key
(cached negative entry, a key racing its own creation, a lookup returning no
rows); the key drops out of keyToId, convert yields nothing, and the allEmpty
branch returned Right (writeAckIds, []) — acking every offset and
dead-lettering nothing. The bytes are gone and no safety net can see it,
because the producer was told it succeeded.

A payload that carried an API key or an at-project-id but produced no rows is
now routed to the DLQ as poison and logged at attention, never acked. This is
the invariant PoisonMsg already documents ("callers MUST publish these to the
DLQ before committing source-topic offsets so the bytes are preserved — never
silent-drop"); it simply was not applied to this case.

Regression test reproduces the exact prod shape: a well-formed OTLP payload
whose only difference is an unresolvable key. Pre-fix it fails with the batch
acked and an empty poison list.

Revert "fix(dashboards): bound TF queries during page render, degrade to client fetch"

This reverts 3615604b1. It caused SIGSEGVs in production.

UnliftIO.timeout delivers an async exception to a thread that may be executing
inside libpq. The PR argued this was safe because resource-pool destroys a
connection whose borrower died — true of the pool's bookkeeping, but it does not
make it safe to unwind a thread mid-libpq-call. Result, from the host kernel log:

  ghc_worker[2343941]: segfault at 55 error 6 in libpq.so.5.15
  ghc_worker[2343346]: segfault ... error 4 in libc.so.6
  ghc_worker[2339831]: segfault ... error 6 in libc.so.6

Address 0x55 is a use-after-free of a PGconn. Four `exit (139)` task failures,
all on this image; the pre-existing image only ever produced exit 1 and 137.

The tell is the timing: the timeout's cancellation path only runs when TF is
slow, so the bug is invisible until exactly the condition the change exists to
handle. It ran clean for ~7h, then crash-looped the moment TF degraded.

Re-land with the SERVER bounding the query instead of the client interrupting it.
TF honours `statement_timeout` (datafusion-postgres reads statement_timeout_ms
from client metadata; verified `SET statement_timeout='7s'` -> `SHOW` = 7000ms).
Note the startup `options=-c statement_timeout=...` route does NOT work — TF
accepts the connection but ignores it (`SHOW` returns 0) — so it must be a `SET`
issued on the session, which implies a dedicated interactive pool so render and
the async /chart_data endpoint can carry different budgets.

Keeps the /ping HEALTHCHECK change out of scope of this revert only because it
lives in the same commit; it was not implicated and should be re-landed with the
corrected fix.

Add monoscope status and monoscope open, and fix summarize-by

Two things a terminal-first user reaches for that were missing:

- `monoscope status` — one screen answering "is anything wrong right now":
  throughput, errors, busiest services, open issues, alerting monitors. A panel
  whose query fails says so inline; an unavailable panel and a quiet one are
  not the same thing.
- `monoscope open <target> [id]` — the web UI link for a trace, issue,
  dashboard, log query or the project, opened or just printed. The host comes
  from /api/v1/me (new `host_url` field) rather than being guessed from the API
  URL, so self-hosted and split API/UI hostnames both work.

Writing status surfaced three real bugs in `summarize <agg> by <field>` with no
time bin — the shape behind `chart --type bar` and the
`summarize count() by resource.service.name` example in our own docs. It failed
for every caller:

1. The grouping column was never projected, so the query returned a bare column
   of numbers with nothing saying which group each belonged to, and no decoder
   accepted it. It now emits (group, aggregate), matching the binned branch.
2. /api/v1/metrics defaulted to the DTMetric decoder, which needs a leading
   timestamp. Charts.decoderFor now infers the decoder from the query shape:
   no `by` → scalar, `by bin(...)` → timeseries, anything else → label/value.
3. `| sort by count_ desc` was silently dropped (the branch hand-rolled its
   ORDER BY), and once aggregates were cast to text for the decoder it would
   have sorted them lexicographically. ORDER BY now resolves aggregation
   aliases back to their expressions, so it sorts numerically.

Hash the Vite entry in its filename instead of a ?v= query

Rollup emits cross-chunk imports back into the entry as a bare
`./index.js` (shared code lives in the entry chunk), so loading the entry
as `index.js?v=<hash>` gave the browser two module identities for the
same file: every page evaluated the component graph twice, and the second
pass threw NotSupportedError on `lit-virtualizer` and `session-replay`.
The un-queried URL was never cache-busted either, so Cloudflare served a
months-old build alongside the current one (max-age=31536000).

Hash the entry filename instead and look the emitted name up through the
Vite build manifest at splice time.

Guard the bundle graph with an e2e spec

Asserts, per page, that each bundle loads exactly once and that nothing
lands in the console. The dedupe compares logical chunk names rather than
URLs — two module graphs built from different revisions collide on name
while every URL stays unique, which is how the ?v= entry bug slipped
through unnoticed.

playwright.config takes E2E_BASE_URL so the suite can be pointed at a
deployed environment; run against prod it fails on all three counts,
naming index/log-list/session-replay as the duplicated bundles.

Route every log/event read to TimeFusion, and let the retry see the error

Two defects on the same read path.

selectLogTable took its TimeFusion routing from whatever the caller
wrapped around it. The log-explorer page wrapped; the public
/api/v1/events handler, the AI tools and the Slack/WhatsApp bots did
not, so they all read Postgres — empty for TF-only projects — and
answered every query with zero rows. Routing is now a parameter of
selectLogTable and its effect row carries Labeled "timefusion" Hasql, so
a caller cannot omit the decision without failing to compile.

isTransientException matched on HasqlException. retryLogExplorerRead
wraps its checkpoint *inside* the retry, so the value the retry inspects
is an AnnotatedException and the match silently never fired: a dropped
TimeFusion connection, already classified transient by
isTransientUsageError, surfaced to the user as "Query execution failed"
(0 "retrying" log lines against 3 qualifying failures today). Matching on
AnnotatedException HasqlException covers both shapes — the instance's
second clause still matches a bare one.

The two other call sites that pass a caught SomeException (Pkg.Queue's
DLQ-vs-retry decision, Telemetry's write retry) are unaffected: their
tryAny sits inside the enclosing checkpoint, which annotates only on the
way out, and nothing on those paths annotates first. They were already
seeing bare exceptions; this keeps them correct if that ever changes.

runQueryEffect now supplies the labeled TimeFusion pool so specs can
exercise the routed path.

Fix the trace waterfall's parent linking, logfmt escaping, and the 90d scan

Found by actually running the commands end-to-end:

- The waterfall keyed the tree on the row UUID, but parent_id holds a *span*
  id (the server aliases context___span_id to latency_breakdown). Every span
  therefore looked like a root and nothing was ever indented. EventRow gains
  spanId and the tree keys on it. The test fixture had encoded the same
  misunderstanding, so it passed throughout — it now carries both ids with the
  real linkage.
- logfmt emitted the summary's ANSI colour codes and did not escape quotes or
  newlines, so a log body containing either split one event across lines. The
  summary is stripped of styling and values are escaped.
- events get --tree hardcoded a 90d scan, which the store can refuse outright
  ("merge-on-read dedup exceeded its per-query limit"). --since narrows it;
  the default is unchanged.

Add service maps; speed up the metrics page

Service maps, global and per-trace, following the OpenTelemetry service-graph
contract: a server/consumer span whose nearest cross-service ancestor is a
client/producer span is one hop between instrumented services, and a
client/producer span nothing answered is a hop into an uninstrumented
dependency (database, queue, third-party host), synthesised as an inferred
node so the map shows the whole system rather than only the parts running our
SDK.

- Global map at /p/:pid/service_map, a third Explorer tab beside Events and
  Metrics. Read from a 5-minute rollup (migration 0117 + odd-jobs dispatcher)
  rather than derived per request: the derivation needs a span self-join, which
  is the query shape that has OOM-killed TimeFusion in production. Gated behind
  ENABLE_SERVICE_MAP_ROLLUP, off by default, pending a smoke test against real
  TimeFusion.
- Map tab in the trace view, derived from spans already on the page, so a
  shared trace link costs no extra query.
- One payload type, one builder and one renderer behind both maps. Rendering is
  echarts' graph series with a deterministic layered left-to-right layout; node
  type is carried by shape plus a dashed border, never colour alone, and the
  same graph renders as a semantic dependency table so a shared link works with
  no JavaScript.
- Explorer tab strip extracted to Utils.explorerNavTabs_; three duplicated
  copies deleted.

Guard the page-chrome globals in the asset spec

Keep the cookie helpers inline so the theme applies before first paint

Moving them into the bundle with the rest of the page chrome broke the theme
block: it calls getCookie while the document is still parsing, so it can set
the saved theme before the first paint. The bundle is a deferred module and
does not run until parsing finishes, so the call threw a ReferenceError and the

else stays in the bundle. The e2e guard now checks both sets, and the jsdom

Unblock deploys: copy shared/ into the image, pin the CapRover CLI

Two independent blockers; production has not been updated since 2026-08-05
02:00 because of them.

Mine: the package split added shared/ and cli/ to cabal.project, but the

node keyed on it is called "0" — accurate and useless on a map. Both the
SQL rollup and inferredPeer now skip a purely numeric namespace and fall
back to db.system, keeping the namespace only when it is a name.

Give the service map Datadog's node styling and click menu

- Labels rendered as "[object Object]". A graph data item's `label` is a field

  object. The display name now travels as `displayName`.
- Nodes are hollow rings rather than filled blobs, labelled to the right. The
  ring carries health (red when failing, the service's own colour otherwise) and
  size stays the only filled signal, which is what keeps a dense graph readable.
- layout:'none' fits the coordinate extent to the box and scales x and y
  independently, so a short chain was stretched edge to edge. The virtual extent
  is floored at the container size, so small graphs draw at their natural
  spacing instead of ballooning.

Only pass -split-sections on Linux; it fails the macOS build

Mach-O dead-strips per symbol via subsections-via-symbols, so GHC ignores
-split-sections there and warns [GHC-74335] — which -Werror turns into a build
failure. macOS x86_64 died on it and took the release job with it; arm64 only
survived because a warm dist-newstyle cache skipped the reconfigure that emits
the warning.

The flag was never doing anything on macOS anyway, which is why that binary is
97MB against Linux's 41MB. Moved to the Linux job, where --gc-sections can
actually use it.

fix(charts): stop freezing an under-returned read into the dashboard forever

A PartialHit fetched only [cachedTo, reqTo], so a bin was read once and never
revisited. One bad read stayed on the customer's chart indefinitely — which is
what turned TimeFusion's bounded-dedup under-count into the recurring
multi-minute holes users reported, long after the rows read correctly again.

The delta now starts at cachedTo minus a trailing overlap so those bins get
re-read and corrected.

That correction relied on "the delta wins on an overlapping bin", which was NOT
actually guaranteed: dedupeByTimestamp keeps the last occurrence after sorting
cached <> new, but the sort was Data.Vector.Algorithms.Intro, which is unstable
— so which value survived an overlapping bin was arbitrary. Switched to
.Merge (stable) and documented why at the import.

Also adds checkReadConsistency to the infra health check, run regardless of
dual-write: a read bug hides stored rows, so neither checkParity nor
checkIngestContinuity can see it, and nothing alerted for the whole incident.
It counts one hour two ways — full-day range + date_trunc pin (full-set dedup)
vs a narrow range (bounded dedup) — and alerts on divergence, reusing the
existing continuityDrop helper. Verified on prod first: 94448 vs 87421 for a
single project-hour.

Don't cast a scalar summarize's aggregate to text

My grouped-summarize fix applied the ::text cast whenever there were
aggregations, including when there was no `by` clause at all. A by-less
summarize is decoded as a float (Charts.decoderFor -> DTFloat), so casting it
made the decode fail: `metrics query 'summarize count()' --assert` and the TF
metric read path both came back "Query execution failed".

Caught by GrpcIngestionSpec 4.4, which only ran once the doctest fix let CI
reach the integration suite. This shipped to prod with the earlier parser
change.

Two unit tests pin both shapes so the cast can't creep back across the
group-by boundary.

Validate KQL field names before the query reaches SQL

A mistyped field reached the database verbatim and came back as
`Schema error: No field named attribute`, logged at ATTENTION and
rendered as a chart overlay. The parser now rejects a subject whose root
names no column, with the nearest match: `Unknown field "attribute". Did
you mean "attributes"?`.

parseQueryDiagnosed keeps the failure position so a caller can point at
the offending text; parseQueryToAST and validateFields are both derived
from it, so there is one rule rather than three. Megaparsec failures are
rendered as one line — errorBundlePretty's caret diagram is unreadable in
a toast, a chart overlay or the strip under the query box.

Three things the parser must not reject, each found by auditing the 1719
queries stored in production:

  - the raw ___ column names (context___trace_id): real columns, used by
    92 saved queries, passed through to SQL unchanged
  - numeric literals in scalar functions (coalesce(status_code, 0)),
    which parse as subjects but name no field
  - a query's own summarize/extend/project outputs, which transformAST
    hoists above the summarize where position can no longer tell them
    from columns

/log_explorer/schema now derives from the same set the parser accepts,
so the query editor cannot squiggle a field the server would take, and
the client needs no second copy of the list.

A post-summarize filter lowers to HAVING with the alias resolved to its

fix(htmx4): migrate event names and drop removed detail fields (#481)

The htmx 4 upgrade left every listener bound to htmx 2 names. The compat
extension replays the camelCase aliases, so most kept working, but the
`hx-on::` attributes did not: an attribute maps `::x` to `htmx:x`
verbatim, and `htmx:before-request` is dispatched by neither htmx 4 nor
the shim. All 8 were inert, which is why the trace details panel stopped
opening. Rename every event to its v4 name so nothing depends on the
shim's replay.

`hx-on::after:settle` on #trace_details_content rather than after:swap:
htmx fires swap events on the requesting element and they bubble, and
that panel is a sibling subtree of the waterfall rows, so after:swap
never reached it. Only the settle pair is dispatched on the swap target.

htmx:afterSettle maps to after:swap, not after:settle: the shim raised
afterSettle from its swap hook, and native after:settle carries
{newContent, settleTasks, task} with no `elt`, which these handlers read.
after:swap preserves both the timing and the detail shape.

Also replace the detail fields v4 removed, which the upgrade checker does
not flag and which were failing silently:

  detail.shouldSwap = false -> event.preventDefault()
  detail.serverResponse     -> detail.ctx.text
  detail.successful         -> detail.ctx.response.status < 400

preventDefault is the only one of these that works; the migration guide's
suggested ctx.target = null does not cancel a swap in 4.0.0-beta6, nor do
detail.cancelled or ctx.swap. Consequences of the dead fields: the AI
search branch in LogQueryBox never ran, two form resets never fired, and
the dashboard widget save both swapped and hand-inserted into gridstack.
