Serve the vitals trend and per-page vitals from one metrics scan

A full-window otel_metrics read is the heaviest query on the RUM page, and
running the two vitals panels as separate scans cost 20s and 48s under
concurrent panel load on the demo project. GROUPING SETS shares one scan
between the per-interval and per-page groupings (verified on TimescaleDB
and TimeFusion), the merged panel is fetched once, and the result is cached
for 15 minutes — per-page P75s move on deploys, not by the minute.

Fetch the sessions panel on row clicks and carry filters on panel shells

Clicking a session row issued a deferred request with no panel, so the
response rendered only shells; hx-select found no workspace in it and the
outerHTML swap deleted the replay workspace from the page. Panel shell URLs
also dropped q/filter/session, so a deep link's panel came back unfiltered
with nothing selected.

Count RUM sessions as distinct ids per interval

The two-stage summarize (min per session, then count per bin) renders a
nonsense total through the chart pipeline's own re-aggregation — the stat
card showed 6149280468.7B sessions. Distinct ids per interval summed counts
a session spanning two intervals twice, a far smaller error.

Attribute in-cluster hostmetrics to the node they measure

A collector agent inside Kubernetes reports host.name as its own pod's
hostname and the measured node only in k8s.node.name — production's exact
shape — so every system.* series either formed a phantom collector host or
dropped out entirely, and all three nodes on the Infrastructure page showed
dashes for CPU, memory, storage, load and uptime while the data sat in the
store. Host identity now prefers k8s.node.name, falls back through the
flattened host.name column to the resource blob, and the datapoint blob
reads accept both nested and flat spellings of dotted attribute keys.

Label uid-only clusters compactly on the Kubernetes tab

A collector that sets no k8s.cluster.name leaves the cluster known only by
uid, and 36 hex characters repeated down every row of the Pods table
identified nothing. Uid-shaped cluster values now render as cluster-<8>,
with the full uid in the tooltip; real names pass through untouched and
filters keep exchanging raw values.

Read blob paths with one operator chain both stores accept

variant_get with a dotted path silently returns NULL for numeric leaves on
TimeFusion, so cpu.logical_number never resolved, the core count came out
NULL, and every host's CPU stayed blank even after the series were correctly
attributed. The -> chain is native JSONB on Postgres and TimeFusion rewrites
it with the numeric-leaf cast, so one spelling now serves both stores and
blobPath loses its dialect flag.

Deflake the metrics catalog keyboard e2e

The service search refreshes its option list 200ms after the last
keystroke; a refresh landing after the test's Space re-rendered the radios
with the pre-selection state, so Search submitted metric_source=all. The
test now lets the refresh settle before selecting and pins the checked
state before submitting — this flake has blocked two green deploys.

Share RUM panel results across replicas through rum_panel_cache

The in-memory panel cache is per replica, so every replica paid each
panel's cold scan once per TTL — the vitals-detail scan alone costs ~25s —
and the first visitor after every expiry always ate one. Panel results now
land in a small keyed table as an L2: memory first, then the shared table,
then the store, so a cold panel is computed at most once per TTL across the
fleet. Expired rows are pruned on write; empty results are still never
cached.

Make the shared-cache example independent of a TimeFusion LIKE bug

The example ingested a 'Pageview \183' span, and TimeFusion's text-index
prefilter currently loses LIKE-matched names inside narrow time windows —
rows the same query returns without the window bounds. That store bug (to
be fixed in timefusion) made the example fail only under TF-backed CI. The
cached-panel mechanics under test are unchanged; the span is now
documentLoad-shaped, which routes through an equality match.

Tighten the inactive-metrics banner and mark the service picker as a filter

The collapsed banner sat at DaisyUI defaults (1rem radius and padding,
plus an mt-4 on top of the page gap); it now uses an 8px radius, compact
title/content padding, and the page gap alone. The All Services summary
gains a filter icon (brand-tinted when a service is selected) and a
chevron so it reads as a dropdown filter like the metric-groups select.

Render the vitals trend through the shared chart widget

The Web Vitals over time panel was the last hand-rolled chart on the RUM
pages. Each vital is now a widget_ timeseries with Google's good/poor marks
as the widget's own threshold lines. The data stays server-computed —
histogram-backed vitals are not expressible in the widget KQL pipeline yet
(value is NULL on histogram datapoints, a gap worth fixing in the metrics
lowering) — and is embedded as the widget's dataset, so it renders like
every other chart without a fetch of its own.

Survive the post-delete redirect race in the dashboard e2e cleanup

The delete handler redirects to the list on its own; a poll goto colliding
with that in-flight redirect aborts (net::ERR_ABORTED), and the abort threw
out of the poll and failed the test — twice in CI today. A failed
navigation now just polls again.

Embed vitals-widget timestamps in milliseconds

The chart axis reads epoch-ms (the data endpoint multiplies before
serving); epoch-seconds silently rendered the 24-hour trend as ninety
seconds of January 1970 wearing today's clock labels.
